value.rationale: Sakai–Akimoto ask when disordered exclusion transport rectifies. This is an exhaustive natural four-site one-vacancy answer: a non-geometric codimension-one family of all-distinct trap rates remains exactly bias-odd at every field, while every profile off the classified surfaces has a global rectification sign. It is a structural symmetry boundary and counterexample to a naive fixed-density generic-rectification expectation, not an arbitrary finite coefficient.
